page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is an x86_64 server belonging to the High Performance family, architected around a 12-vCPU configuration with 24 GB of RAM. The instance allocates 12 virtual cores across 6 physical cores on a shared 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor, providing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB per virtual core, establishing a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Fast primary storage is directly bundled through a 500 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements demonstrate distinct multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread metrics. In parallel computational tasks, the instance delivers solid performance, achieving average relative ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Cache-resident read memory bandwidth reaches 1019.76 GB/sec, and uncached sequential read operations sustain 79.14 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing exhibits limitations, marked by weak scores in Geekbench single-core and lower-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and text manipulation workloads.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the provision of 12 virtual cores and integrated 500 GB NVMe storage provides practical compute density for concurrent workloads that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. Tradeoffs center on shared CPU scheduling and constrained single-thread clock speed, which limit suitability for latency-sensitive single-threaded pipelines or large-scale in-memory databases. The server is practical for parallel code compilation, CI/CD pipeline workers, static web servers, backend microservice clusters, and batch data processing.
description: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is a compute-aligned virtual server instance configured with 12 shared vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, the instance couples its multi-core CPU architecture with 24 GB of system RAM and 500 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, omitting dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal moderate multi-threaded throughput, registering average outcomes across stress-ng, Clang software compilation, and Redis operations, while single-core processing metrics, such as compression algorithms and text parsing, position lower against competing architectures. The combination of dense multi-core provisioning and fast local storage delivers solid compute economy for parallelized jobs. The server is well matched for software build farms, parallel batch processing, static web serving clusters, and containerized microservices that benefit from multi-threaded concurrency without requiring disproportionate memory allocations.
